doc_verification.detail: Reachability: WebFetch was domain-blocked for api.qdrant.tech, but the alternate mcp web reader fetched both the HTML page and the .md version successfully (canonical URL https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/distributed/recover-current-peer) -> PASS. Version: page header shows 'v1.18.x', URL segment v-1-18-x; target v1.18.0 major.minor match -> PASS. Content: the v1.18.x page documents POST /cluster/recover with description 'Attempts to restore or synchronize the node's current state with that of its peers.', NO request body parameters, and exactly one documented response '200 successful operation' (usage/time/status/result envelope); no 4xx/5xx documented and no standalone/distributed-mode precondition stated on this page — the contract expected_behavior 'HTTP 200 on cluster recovery' matches the sole documented response; nuance (not a FAIL): the contract description's 'intended for use only when quorum is permanently lost' and the endpoint_registry doc_quote are not verbatim on the current v1.18.x page (provenance likely older OpenAPI/distributed docs; in-tree openapi/openapi-cluster.ytt.yaml:38-44 has summary 'Tries to recover current peer Raft state.' with a single boolean response). Endpoint precision: registry path cluster+recover -> POST /cluster/recover at the same source_url, confirmed by the doc page -> PASS.

http_semantics.note: No 2xx masking of a client error occurred. The observed 500 is a server-state (deployment-mode) ServiceError, not a request-side-decidable error: malformed/extreme bodies never produced any client-error signal because the REST handler never reads the request body at all (source-verified: recover_current_peer in cluster_api.rs has no body extractor), and even the documented no-body control returns the same 500. Malformed-input disposition is therefore unobservable on this endpoint in this deployment. Response latencies are microseconds (0.00011-0.00048 s), consistent with an immediate mode-gate rejection, not body processing.

log: VERDICT DEFECT_FOUND (Type3_RuntimeFailure); raw response verified — HTTP 500 {"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode"}} with /healthz 200 after every probe; the 500 is authentic and the documented 200 was not returned

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST POST /cluster/recover -> recover_current_peer (src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:60, handler takes only dispatcher+auth, NO body extractor -> request body never read, so payload size/content cannot influence this path) -> Dispatcher.toc() -> TableOfContent::request_snapshot() (lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/mod.rs:546) -> get_consensus_proposal_sender() (toc/mod.rs:775) -> consensus_proposal_sender is None when settings.cluster.enabled == false (set at src/main.rs:508-514 with explicit comment 'We don't need sender for the single-node mode') -> StorageError::service_error("Qdrant is running in standalone mode") -> Display 'Service internal error: {description}' (errors.rs:21) -> mapped to StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (src/actix/helpers.rs:247). Fully explains the observed body and the identical 500 across all 4 probes and the no-body control. The 200 documented path requires a consensus sender, i.e. a distributed-mode deployment; the sandbox deployment self-reported GET /cluster {"result":{"status":"disabled"}} (log line 6).

mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode gate: the sandbox runs Qdrant single-node (cluster.enabled=false; GET /cluster self-reports status 'disabled'), so every consensus-dependent operation — including /cluster/recover, whose REST handler never reads the body — deterministically returns StorageError::service_error('Qdrant is running in standalone mode') mapped to HTTP 500. The by_design_in_source marking is scoped: the single-node None choice carries the explicit maintainer comment 'We don't need sender for the single-node mode' (main.rs:513), and the mode gate fully explains the 500; however the CHOICE of HTTP 500 (ServiceError) rather than a 4xx for this mode gate on this endpoint has no explicit intent annotation in source, and the script's declared resource-limit/DoS mechanism (body-induced OOM/hang) is disconfirmed by source (handler never reads the body) and by the sibling no-body control returning the identical 500. Whether the deployment-mode gate defeats the defect claim (undocumented 500 vs documented-only 200 on a distributed-mode operation tested against a standalone deployment) is left to the auditor.

contract_grounding_note: api_violates_assertion=true reasoning: the claim's phenomenon is an undocumented 500 (not silent acceptance). The quoted assertion (verbatim substring of the contract description field: 'returns 200 ok; intended for use only when quorum is permanently lost'; the contract's expected_behavior field additionally reads 'HTTP 200 on cluster recovery (dangerous operational op)') promises a 200 outcome; the observed response for the documented, body-less operation form is HTTP 500 with a structured service error, and no request-side illegality exists (even the no-body control 500s, sibling log 002:7). Therefore the observed behavior does not satisfy the quoted expectation — violation is genuine on the literal doc face; the mitigating deployment-mode context is recorded under mundane_explanation.surviving for the auditor's by-design weighing.
